answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via key-bound memory-hard proof-of-work. Each epoch, agents solve a RAM-bound puzzle tied to their public key and a beacon within a tight time delta. Because each key builds a unique memory table, attackers cannot reuse work and incur the verifiable cost of dedicated DRAM and energy per identity, spacing accounts like berths at a wharf so each stays scarce as a pearl. However, botnets or rented cloud nodes can still fund brief fake swarms.
